svg.text: Poker Table Helper v3 — rethought
AMOLED black · colour only on buttons that need a tap · glanceable complications · iPhone 18 Pro (402 × 874 pt) · numbers are illustrative
1. Setup — one decision
You only pick the dealer. You are always the
bottom seat, so SB/BB are derived (heads-up:
dealer = SB).
Seats drawn like your real table, numbered
clockwise from you — natural mapping (Norman).
Stack set once; the app tracks every chip after
that (all-ins, side pots, rebuys).

g.text: Tap the dealer. Blinds follow automatically.

svg.text: 2. Card entry — marking menu
Press-slide-release = rank + suit in one stroke.
Marking menus: marks 3–7× faster than menu picks
once learned (Kurtenbach & Buxton).
Tap-tap still works, so it’s easy on day one.
Keypad sits mid-screen, the most accurate touch
zone (Hoober). Cards already in play are greyed
out.

g.text: Press a rank, slide to a suit, lift. One gesture per card.
Or tap rank, then tap suit. Used cards are locked.

svg.text: 3. Logging a friend’s move
Buttons are outlined, not lit: you are recording
someone else’s move, so no advice is shown on
them.
Check and Call share one button — they are never
both legal (Hick’s law: fewer choices, faster
picks).
Undo sits beside the buttons: mistakes get fixed
where they happen (Fitts’s law).
4. Your turn — the best move glows
Only the best move lights up: one pre-attentive
cue you can read in a glance. The others show
their EV so you see how close it is.
Four complications, one number each (Win, Need,
EV, SPR). Tap any one for the full maths.
Buttons are 96 pt tall in the lower-middle band;
edges need ≥11–12 mm targets vs 7 mm in the centre
(Hoober).
5. Raise — press and pull up
Press RAISE and pull up: one continuous gesture,
thumb never leaves the glass. Release to set, tap
the amount to type it exactly.
Log-scale track: sizes feel like ratios, so
Min→Pot gets as much travel as Pot→All-in. Detents
tick with iOS haptics.
Live readout sits above-left of the thumb so your
finger never covers it; EV and fold % update while
you drag.

g.text: Tap to type an exact amount

svg.text: 6. Exact amount — keypad
Custom raises are first class: type the exact
chips. Anything below a legal min-raise or above
your stack is blocked, not silently fixed.
EV and fold % recalculate on every keypress, so
you can test a size before committing.
Shortcuts for the sizes you use most; All-in in
amber, the one colour reserved for “everything”.
7. Tap a complication — the maths
Heads-up equity is exact (every remaining card),
multiway shows ± error from sampling. Nothing is
rounded into a guess.
Each friend’s range starts from their own VPIP/PFR
and is re-weighted by every bet they make
(Bayesian, like the Alberta Poki bot).
Every action and size gets an EV in big blinds;
the formula is shown, not hidden.

g.text: Seat 9: VPIP 31%, PFR 14% over 24 hands; bet on K-9-4 keeps 61 combos
You have 71.2%, so calling wins chips; raising wins more.

svg.text: 8. Showdown — pots resolve themselves
Side pots are built from the all-ins
automatically; you only tap who won each one
(split = tap two).
Or enter the cards people show and the evaluator
decides, including kickers and split pots.
Stacks update, the hand is logged for each
friend’s stats, the button moves.
